message.content:
Civil law, also known as civil jurisprudence or civil law system, is a legal framework that governs non-criminal disputes between private parties. Its components can be broadly categorized into several key areas: | Component | Description | |-----------|-------------| | **Sources of Law** | • **Statutes & Codes** – Written laws enacted by legislatures (e.g., Civil Code, Commercial Code).
• **Case Law / Precedent** – Judicial decisions that interpret statutes and establish legal principles.
• **Customary Law** – Long‑standing practices recognized as binding in certain jurisdictions.
• **Doctrine & Academic Writings** – Scholarly works that influence interpretation and development of law. | | **Legal Subjects** | • **Persons** – Natural persons, legal entities (companies, NGOs), and sometimes quasi‑persons (e.g., corporations).
• **Property** – Real property, movable property, intellectual property, and intangible assets.
• **Contracts** – Agreements, obligations, and their enforcement.
• **Torts / Delicts** – Wrongful acts causing harm or loss.
• **Family Law** – Marriage, divorce, child custody, adoption.
• **Succession / Inheritance** – Distribution of estates after death. | | **Procedural Elements** | • **Jurisdiction** – Determining which court has authority over a case.
• **Venue** – The specific location where a case is heard.
• **Pleadings** – Complaint, answer, counterclaim, etc.
• **Evidence Rules** – Admissibility, burden of proof, standard of proof.
• **Judgment & Remedies** – Damages, injunctions, specific performance, restitution. | | **Legal Principles** | • **Good Faith & Fair Dealing** – Parties must act honestly and fairly.
• **Contractual Freedom** – Parties can generally choose terms within legal limits.
• **Responsibility & Liability** – Conditions under which parties owe duties and can be held liable.
• **Equitable Remedies** – Remedies based on fairness rather than strict legal rules. | | **Specialized Areas** | • **Commercial Law** – Business transactions, corporate governance, bankruptcy.
• **Consumer Protection** – Rights of buyers and sellers, product liability.
• **Environmental Law** – Regulations protecting natural resources.
• **Labor & Employment Law** – Rights and duties of employers and employees. | | **Enforcement Mechanisms** | • **Court System** – Trial courts, appellate courts, supreme courts.
• **Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR)** – Mediation, arbitration, conciliation.
• **Administrative Agencies** – Bodies that enforce specific regulations (e.g., consumer protection agencies). | These components interact to form a comprehensive system that addresses disputes, protects rights, and promotes social order in civil matters.
